newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends lower on state bank covering.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends lower on state bank covering.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee edged lower on Monday on import covering by a state bank, ending at 55.74 to the dollar after openening at 55.67, dealers said.
"The dollar hit a high of 55.75 on import covering by a state bank before easing slightly," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
With the dollar remaining firm overseas, the Central Bank quoted the U.S. unit higher by 3.75 local cents in the morning, setting buying and selling at 55.4252 and 56.5449 respectively.
Overnight call money closed at 14.25 percent after trading in a tight range, dealers said. It was 14.50 percent on Friday.
The govenrment has indicated it will raise 500 million rupees at this week's T-bill auction on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The money market is waiting to see what impact this will have on rates," sid a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
